title: Find the Index of Permutation
summary: Determine the position of a given permutation array perm within the lexicographically ordered list of all permutations of [1, 2, ..., n], and provide the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Determine the position of a given permutation array perm within the lexicographically ordered list of all permutations of [1, 2, ..., n], and provide the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: perm is a permutation of integers 1 through n.
Index all permutations in zero-based lexicographic order.
reference_solution:
def permutation_lexicographic_index(perm):
    modulo=1000000007;size=len(perm);tree=[0]*(size+1);factorial=[1]*size
    for index in range(1,size):factorial[index]=factorial[index-1]*index%modulo
    def add(index):
        while index<=size:tree[index]+=1;index+=index&-index
    def used_through(index):
        total=0
        while index:total+=tree[index];index-=index&-index
        return total
    answer=0
    for index,value in enumerate(perm):
        smaller_unused=value-1-used_through(value)
        answer=(answer+smaller_unused*factorial[size-index-1])%modulo
        add(value)
    return answer

hints: At each position, every smaller unused value starts a block of (remaining length)! earlier permutations.
Use a Fenwick tree to count used values and precompute factorials modulo the target.

Lexicographic blocks partition all earlier permutations by their first differing position, so summing their sizes gives the exact zero-based rank.

The four earlier permutations begin with one or two, so [3,1,2] has index four.
